correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the coprime annihilator criterion from the definition. For a nonzero coprime ideal, localization at a maximal support prime and Nakayama show containment in all nonzero local maximal-ideal powers; Krull intersection forces local nilpotence. The selected maximal/minimal prime splits off as a clopen Artinian local factor, and join-primality forces the ideal into this factor. Artinian local annihilators and Nakayama make coprimality equivalent to inclusion in every nonzero ideal, and this happens for exactly the unique one-dimensional socle of an Artinian Gorenstein factor. Orthogonal supports give all closed subsets. Verified all hypotheses (Noetherian, finitely generated ideals, local nilpotence, field case, empty case). Brute-force independent-of-classification algebra computations test the defining condition in 17 small Artinian configurations. Infinite Noetherian assertion relies on proof, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The introduced coprime ideal definition, annihilator criterion, dual-ring equivalence, and domain special case are credited to arXiv:2609.23351. The present theorem classifies every commutative Noetherian ring, including mixtures with positive-dimensional and non-Gorenstein factors, by exact Artinian Gorenstein component selection; no inspected source or relevant indexed record stated or implied that universal classification. Explicit residual risks are recorded, so the negative search is not treated as a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Completes the classification of a recently introduced invariant across all commutative Noetherian rings. It identifies a structural Gorenstein component selector, gives an exact cardinality and a strong finite-discrete topological rigidity theorem, and explains the sharp contrast with the motivating non-Noetherian Sierpinski example. It makes the invariant computable from a canonical decomposition and distinguishes field, Gorenstein, non-Gorenstein, positive-dimensional, and mixed cases; this is not an arbitrary special case or a mere new numerical sample.
